content: Before starting dolutegravir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you are pregnant, notify your doctor before using this medication, as treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Be aware that this medication can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (such as liver and kidney function, viral load, and T-cell counts) should be conducted. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. For 10-milligram tablets, keep them in their original container with the drying agent (desiccant) inside. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
